blocks.narration: Justin Gaethje stopped Ilia Topuria at UFC Freedom 250 in June, and now the lightweight champion refuses the rematch and won't say if he fights again. So is the champion really walking away? It starts with Topuria's comment about Gaethje's gloves, and on the Flagrant podcast, Gaethje answers it.

Then, Chael Sonnen weighs in on the glove controversy and the official response around the fight. He says the commission looked into Justin Gaethje’s gloves and explains why the cheating angle did not hold up.
On the other side, Paddy Pimblett weighs in on Ilia Topuria’s accusation against Justin Gaethje. He presents it as an excuse and uses the moment to attack Topuria’s character after the title fight.

Adding to that, Justin Gaethje doubles down on why he does not believe Ilia Topuria deserves another title shot. He focuses on Topuria’s body breaking down and explains why he sees the finish differently than Topuria does.

Taking that further, Justin Gaethje lays out what he thinks happened to Ilia Topuria mentally after the loss. He says Topuria built a belief around being unbeatable and now has to rebuild that reality after June.

However, Justin Gaethje admits his own future is still unsettled after becoming UFC lightweight champion at 37. He points to injuries, age, and a career that began in 2008 as reasons he has not decided.

Beyond that, Justin Gaethje rejects the idea that retirement talk is only a negotiation tactic. He says the decision is about his health rather than money, even with major title options still on the table.

At the same time, Justin Gaethje points toward Arman Tsarukyan as the clear next contender. Tsarukyan knocked out Mauricio Ruffy at UFC 331, but Gaethje says injuries keep him from fighting again this year.

Then, Justin Gaethje reveals where communication stands with the UFC after winning the belt. He says he has fought twice in six months and shuts down the idea that Arman Tsarukyan can get him in January.
On a similar note, Justin Gaethje discusses the money being thrown around him outside the cage. He talks about corner offers and makes clear that loyalty to his team matters more than a number.

However, Ariel Helwani questions whether Justin Gaethje is really ready to walk away from the best position of his career. He points to possible fights with Arman Tsarukyan, Ilia Topuria, and Paddy Pimblett.

From Daniel Cormier’s side, the biggest money question is complicated by Conor McGregor. Cormier says beating Ilia Topuria may actually push Gaethje away from a McGregor fight, while the champion remains 37 and undecided.
Adding to that, Daniel Cormier rejects the idea of Justin Gaethje vacating as champion for a money fight. He says the belt changes the equation, even if retirement is still a serious possibility.

At the same time, Chael Sonnen puts Arman Tsarukyan forward as the rightful number one contender. He still says giving Ilia Topuria another title shot would not be unfair, but predicts Gaethje versus Arman next.

Then, Michael Bisping highlights where he believes the UFC lightweight title picture is going. He predicts an announcement for Justin Gaethje against Arman Tsarukyan before the end of the year, with Paddy Pimblett facing Topuria.
Meanwhile, Paddy Pimblett keeps himself in the conversation by laying out the fights he wants most. He says he would pick Gaethje for the belt, Topuria for a grudge fight, and Arman Tsarukyan later.
On the other side, Paddy Pimblett directly calls for Ilia Topuria while saying he has no fight booked. He also floats a TUF season and predicts a quick win if the matchup is made.

Beyond that, Justin Gaethje doubles down on his view that Ilia Topuria is not built for lightweight. He names Paddy Pimblett and Arman Tsarukyan while predicting Topuria will not become champion at 155.

Taking that further, Justin Gaethje explains why he thinks future lightweights will handle Ilia Topuria differently. He argues that opponents will stop walking into Topuria’s punches the same way after seeing the loss.

Finally, Justin Gaethje lays out the two obvious paths in front of him after winning the lightweight title. He says the choice is retirement or Arman Tsarukyan, but for now he is recovering and enjoying being champion.

titles: “HE SHOULD HAVE QUIT ON THE STOOL!” Justin Gaethje SHUTS DOWN Ilia Topuria Rematch!
“HE HAS TO BELIEVE THAT I CHEATED!” Justin Gaethje FIRES BACK At Ilia Topuria’s Glove Claim!
“I’D SEND HIM BACK TO FEATHERWEIGHT!” Paddy Pimblett CALLS OUT Ilia Topuria After Gaethje Loss!
“THERE WAS NOTHING ILLEGAL IN THE GLOVES!” Chael Sonnen ENDS Topuria’s Cheating Claim!
“THERE’S ABSOLUTELY NO WAY HE’S WALKING AWAY!” Ariel Helwani CALLS BS On Gaethje Retirement Talk!
description:
Justin Gaethje is refusing an Ilia Topuria rematch after stopping him at UFC Freedom 250, and the fallout now includes Topuria’s glove-check comment, Gaethje’s response, and questions about whether the champion fights again.

Arman Tsarukyan is waiting after knocking out Mauricio Ruffy at UFC 331, Paddy Pimblett wants Topuria next, and analysts are split on whether Gaethje returns, retires, or takes the biggest offer available.

Credits: Flagrant Clips, One Night with Steiny, Kolos MMA, Michael Bisping, Daniel Cormier, The Ariel Helwani Show, Chael Sonnen.
pinned_comment: Should Justin Gaethje fight Arman Tsarukyan next, give Ilia Topuria the rematch, or retire as champion?
outro: Justin Gaethje says Ilia Topuria does not deserve a rematch, while Arman Tsarukyan, Paddy Pimblett, and the money fights all wait for an answer. What happens next could reshape the division. So, drop your thoughts below.
